title: Microsoft Teams: mandatory pre-meeting consent for meeting participants
summary: The briefing's controls, default and rollout statements are supported by the documentation and Microsoft's tenant notice. It correctly distinguishes the general Teams licence requirement from unpublished feature-specific licensing, and explicitly reports the conflicting preview and release statements.

claims.claim: Teams supports an admin-configured custom consent message that participants accept before joining meetings.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can configure a custom consent message that participants must accept before they can join meetings hosted by organizers in your organization.

claims.claim: Consent content can include terms and conditions, disclaimers, recording notices or responsible AI usage guidelines.
claims.quote: You can present custom terms and conditions, disclaimers, recording notices, responsible AI usage guidelines, and other compliance-related statements to meeting participants.

claims.claim: The feature's Learn page still marks it as Public Preview, unlike the roadmap and tenant notice.
claims.quote: This feature is currently in Public Preview.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference says EnablePreMeetingConsent has no effect because the feature is not fully released.
claims.quote:
-EnablePreMeetingConsent
Controls whether participants must explicitly accept a custom consent dialog before they can join any meeting hosted by the tenant.
This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference gives the same no-effect warning for PreMeetingConsentContentIdentifier.
claims.quote:
-PreMeetingConsentContentIdentifier
A string identifier that references the Id of the PreMeetingConsentContent configuration stored as meeting settings.
This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.

claims.where: Scope: Roles and prerequisites; What's changing
claims.claim: The feature guide documents configuration through both the Teams admin center and PowerShell.
claims.quote: You can enable and configure pre-meeting consent in the Teams admin center or by using PowerShell.

claims.claim: The feature page marks pre-meeting consent as applying to Meetings, not Events.
claims.quote: APPLIES TO: [checkmark for yes] Meetings [x for No] Events

claims.claim: The enable control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting join & lobby > Enable pre-meeting participant consent.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
Under Meeting join & lobby, turn the Enable pre-meeting participant consent toggle On.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -EnablePreMeetingConsent $true is the documented enabling call, with the reference's no-effect caveat reported in the body.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy
[[-Identity] <XdsIdentity>]
[-EnablePreMeetingConsent <Boolean>]
$true: All participants must explicitly accept a custom consent dialog before joining any meeting hosted by the tenant.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: The returned consent configuration identifier is assigned to a meeting policy using Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -PreMeetingConsentContentIdentifier.
claims.quote:
Copy the configuration identifier returned by New-CsPreMeetingConsent:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy `
    -Identity $policyIdentity `
    -PreMeetingConsentContentIdentifier $consentId `
    -EnablePreMeetingConsent $true
